purpose: Model how observations, ideas, drafts, experiments, claims, and projects acquire stronger institutional state while preserving provenance, evidence, ownership, defects, and the ability to reopen work when later conditions invalidate closure.
provenanceNote: The state model is the Lab Machine's operational projection. Current-work placement is derived from the source project index and is intentionally labeled as a projection rather than silently replacing each project's native operatingState and projectPhase.

states.label: Captured
states.role: The object exists in a durable intake boundary instead of only in conversation, memory, or transient output.
entryConditions: an identifiable observation, idea, request, draft, source, or anomaly exists
enough provenance is attached to recover where it came from
exitSignals: the object can be classified without inventing missing context
a next responsible action or investigation can be named

states.label: Triaged
states.role: The object has a type, scope, standing, priority, and routing decision sufficient to enter deliberate work.
entryConditions: intake object is identifiable
scope and obvious duplicates or exclusions have been checked
exitSignals: the work belongs to a known program or bounded queue
ownership or stewardship expectations are visible
the investigation question is sharper than the intake label

states.label: Researching
states.role: Evidence, domain structure, alternatives, prior art, constraints, and failure conditions are being developed.
entryConditions: a bounded question exists
relevant sources or test environments can be named
exitSignals: material evidence and contradictions are represented
the next representation or experiment is justified
major unknowns are explicit rather than silently assumed

states.label: Structured
states.role: The work has been converted into an inspectable representation with typed objects, relations, procedure, claim boundary, or implementation skeleton.
entryConditions: research has produced enough distinctions to justify a representation
the representation declares what it leaves unresolved
exitSignals: another person or agent can reconstruct the object
tests, comparisons, or implementation can operate on the representation
dependencies and expected invariants are visible

states.label: Testing
states.role: The representation is being forced to answer through execution, comparison, reconstruction, counterexample, review experiment, or matched baseline.
entryConditions: a testable proposition or executable path exists
success and failure signals are declared
exitSignals: observations are recorded
defects and counterevidence are attached
the evidence is sufficient to justify review or another repair loop

states.label: Reviewing
states.role: A distinct witness evaluates evidence, scope, maturity, contradiction, authority, and unresolved obligations before stronger state is granted.
entryConditions: test or research evidence exists
material inference and known failures are visible
exitSignals: review decision is attributable
required repairs are either completed or explicitly block promotion
claim ceiling and intended audience are declared

states.label: Promoted
states.role: A bounded object has acquired stronger institutional standing for a declared purpose without becoming universally true, final, or immutable.
entryConditions: required evidence and review gates passed
authority to promote is attributable
replacement and repair behavior are defined
exitSignals: the stronger object has a stable address, status, owner, and dependency record
release, deployment, publication, or reuse can proceed without hiding its maturity

states.label: Published / Deployed
states.role: The promoted object has crossed an external or operational boundary and can now create public, user, institutional, or system consequence.
entryConditions: release audience and consequence boundary are understood
operational or publication prerequisites are met
exitSignals: the object is reachable in its intended environment
observation, feedback, incident, citation, or use can be attached
repair ownership remains live

states.label: Maintained
states.role: The institution continues to own validity, availability, revision, provenance, dependency, and repair obligations after initial release or closure.
entryConditions: a promoted or released object remains relevant enough to retain
a steward or maintenance rule exists
exitSignals: the object remains current within its declared scope
supersession, archive, or reopening can be executed without losing history

states.label: Reopened / Repair
states.role: New evidence, defect, dependency change, incident, contradiction, or changed context has invalidated part of a later state and routed the work back into an explicit repair loop.
entryConditions: a later-state object no longer satisfies a protected condition
the affected scope or dependency can be identified
exitSignals: repair target and owner are named
affected downstream objects are queued
the object returns to the earliest state required by the defect rather than restarting blindly

gates.label: Admissibility
gates.question: Does this object belong, and can it be bounded without inventing context?
gates.failureRoute: Retain as unresolved intake, merge with an existing object, or exclude with an explicit reason.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.question: Is there enough grounded structure to justify making a stronger representation?
gates.failureRoute: Return to research; do not let structural neatness substitute for evidence.

gates.label: Testability
gates.question: Can this representation be made to answer?
gates.failureRoute: Repair the representation until the test can distinguish success from fluent restatement.

gates.label: Review
gates.question: Is the evidence package complete enough for an independent or role-separated witness to judge?
gates.failureRoute: Remain in testing or return to research/structure with the missing evidence obligation recorded.

gates.label: Promotion Authority
gates.question: Who is allowed to give this object stronger institutional standing, and on what evidence?
gates.failureRoute: Bounded refusal or return to the earliest failed gate; generation quality does not supply authority.

gates.label: Release
gates.question: May this object cross into public or operational consequence?
gates.failureRoute: Keep the object promoted internally or revise the release projection without lowering the evidence record.

gates.label: Stewardship
gates.question: Who owns the object after the launch moment?
checks: feedback and defects have an intake route
gates.failureRoute: Do not treat release as closure; assign ownership or explicitly archive the object.

items.title: Boundary Theory Node Reorganization
items.summary: Reorganize the canonical node ontology around Boundary Theory, Distinction Space, primary theory facets, Representational Mechanics, Formal Grammars, Boundary First, and Boundary-First Engineering.
items.mappingNote: The source project is complete in closure; the pipeline projection places it in Maintained because its outputs now function as retained canonical infrastructure rather than active discovery work.

items.title: Boundary First Labs Introductory Experience
items.summary: Build a guided, resumable first passage that teaches the atlas legend before revealing the full map.
items.mappingNote: Definition work already has explicit wireframes and config outputs, so the projection places it in Structured while preserving the source phase as definition.

items.title: Corpus Forge Agent Pipeline
items.summary: Configure and test the supervised Operator-Critic-Human promotion workflow for corpus refinement.
items.mappingNote: The source phase is validation, which maps directly to Testing in the institutional projection. Promotion is deliberately not inferred.

items.title: Boundary-First Soccer Theory Development
items.summary: Develop soccer as a continuous, noisy, multi-agent public on-ramp for Boundary First and Representational Mechanics.
items.mappingNote: This remains candidate research and definition work, so the projection keeps it in Researching rather than treating the existence of a theory document as promotion.

items.title: Software Before Code Publication Development
items.summary: Develop the practitioner-facing publication that explains software as representation, executable process, closure, and consequence.
items.mappingNote: The work has a public working method and retained source material but still identifies comparative validation as future work; Structured is therefore stronger than intake but weaker than validated promotion.

items.title: AI as Forge Follow-up Series
items.summary: Develop a public follow-up series explaining AI-assisted transformation, provenance, critique, and closure gates.
items.mappingNote: Although the source projectPhase says publication, operatingState is planned. The pipeline projection therefore keeps it at Captured until active work supplies evidence for a stronger state.
